questions.q: Why does tabular Q-learning fail to scale to problems like Atari gameplay from pixels?
options: The reward signal is always zero in Atari games
The state space is too large or continuous for a table to enumerate every entry
Q-learning only works with continuous actions
Atari environments are not Markov decision processes
questions.explain: A Q-table needs one row per state-action pair. High-dimensional or continuous state spaces, like raw pixel frames, make that enumeration impossible, motivating function approximation.

questions.q: In DQN, what does the neural network Q(s, a; theta) compute?
options: A probability distribution over next states
One Q-value per possible action, given a state
The optimal policy directly as a one-hot action vector
The reward function for the environment
questions.explain: The Q-network takes a state as input and outputs an estimated Q-value for every action, just as a row of the Q-table would.

questions.q: What is the TD target used in the DQN loss function?
options: r + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a'; theta_minus)
The average reward over the whole episode
Q(s, a; theta) with no reward term
The policy's entropy at the next state
questions.explain: DQN regresses Q(s, a; theta) toward r + gamma times the max next-state Q-value, evaluated using the target network's weights theta_minus.

questions.q: Why is training a Q-network directly on an agent's raw, sequential experience unstable?
options: Neural networks cannot represent Q-functions
The data is correlated rather than independent, and the regression target shifts as theta updates
Gradient descent cannot be used for regression problems
The discount factor must always equal 1
questions.explain: Sequential transitions are highly correlated, and because the target network's weights move with theta in the naive version, the thing being regressed toward keeps changing.

questions.q: What does the (1 - dones) term do in the DQN target computation?
options: It doubles the learning rate at the end of an episode
It zeroes out the bootstrapped next-state value at terminal transitions
It selects which action was taken
It normalizes the reward to between 0 and 1
questions.explain: When a transition ends an episode, there is no next state to bootstrap from, so multiplying the next-state value term by (1 - dones) correctly drops it from the target.
